claim_entries.value: explanations during or after the ride turn reported UX from negative to neutral, possibly through increased perceived control (PDF p. 1).
quotes: "The AVAM questionnaire, UEQ-S and interviews show that explanations during or after the ride help turn a negative user experience into a neutral one, which might be due to the increased feeling of control." (p. 1)

claim_entries.value: performance — the claim concerns an intervention effect on reported UX and control (PDF p. 1).
quotes: "The AVAM questionnaire, UEQ-S and interviews show that explanations during or after the ride help turn a negative user experience into a neutral one, which might be due to the increased feeling of control." (p. 1)

claim_entries.value: empirical — the paper reports a user study of explanations during and after a simulated autonomous ride (PDF p. 1).
quotes: "We conducted a user study to determine whether explanations of the system during or after an autonomous ride can improve the experience with the AV, or even support passengers’ well-being." (p. 1)

claim_entries.value: mixed_factorial — the app comparison is within-participant and live explanation is between groups (PDF p. 6).
quotes: "We then asked participants to interact with the app." (p. 6)
"For these reasons, we chose an independent control group without live explanations but retrospective explanations." (p. 6)

claim_entries.value: 40 — twenty participants were assigned to each group (PDF p. 3).
quotes: "Overall, 40 participants were individually taking part in the experiment, 20 participants in each of the following groups:" (p. 3)

claim_entries.value: mixed — the sample combined industry employees, students, and university or research-campus employees (PDF p. 3).
quotes: "The participant group consisted of employees of a German automobile manufacturer, students and employees of a university as well as employees of a research campus." (p. 3)

claim_entries.value: control_condition — the live-explanation group was compared with an original-scene group (PDF p. 3).
quotes: "Group A watched the original version of the scene recording." (p. 3)
"Group B watched the scene that was enhanced by simultaneous explanatory information (live explanation):" (p. 3)

claim_entries.value: test_only — the inferential comparisons report named tests and significance but no comparison effect size (PDF p. 6).
quotes: "Therefore, a Wilcoxon Signed Ranks test was performed for the dependent samples and a Mann-Whitney test for the independent samples instead of an ANOVA." (p. 6)

claim_entries.value: 30 minutes on average; ride 8 minutes 25 seconds (PDF p. 4).
quotes: "For each participant, the experiment lasted 30 minutes on average." (p. 4)
"As part of the experiment, the overall driving time in the shuttle prototype was 8 minutes 25 seconds which is equivalent to an average taxi ride in Germany [3]." (p. 4)

claim_entries.value: perceived safety and interest were unsupported, and adding the app after live explanation produced no increased UX (PDF pp. 6–7).
quotes: "Using the application after the drive with additional explanatory information produced almost the same results and did not show an increased UX." (p. 7)
"Hence, there is no evidence that supports hypothesis H1.1." (p. 6)
"Hence, there is no evidence that supports hypothesis H1.3 from the experiment." (p. 7)

claim_entries.value: the between-group live-explanation contrast and within-participant app contrast support the bounded claim about immediate reported UX in this simulator, while the paper does not claim learning or transfer (PDF pp. 7, 10).
quotes: "Overall, group B, where live explanations were provided, had higher ratings in ease of use and understanding of the system than group A." (p. 7)
"Also, as the visual enhancements on the displays were done manually, the intended route and marked items were perfectly highlighted without errors." (p. 10)

paper_code_entries.value: passenger sensemaking and user experience during autonomous driving (PDF p. 1).
quotes: "This paper focusses on vehicles with full driving automation (SAE level 5 [43]) and investigates if system explanations can improve the UX during autonomous rides." (p. 1)

paper_code_entries.value: immediate_performance_or_sensemaking — the explanations support experience and perceived control during or directly after the ride (PDF p. 1).
quotes: "Using a driving simulator and a mobile application, we evaluated if system transparency during and after the interaction can increase the user experience and subjective feeling of safety and control." (p. 1)

paper_code_entries.value: mixed_or_transitioning — the sample spans no prior autonomous-system experience through limited fully autonomous-vehicle experience (PDF p. 3).
quotes: "Based on their prior experiences with autonomous systems, participants are distributed in: 25% had no prior experiences, 50% had experiences with driving assistance such as cruise control, 12.5% had experiences with semi-automatic driving systems such as lane assists, 5% had experiences with highly automated driving systems such as highway and take-over driving assistants, and 7.5% had experiences with fully autonomous vehicles in research contexts." (p. 3)

paper_code_entries.value: knowledge_or_concept_gap — passengers may not understand autonomous-driving behaviour without explanatory information (PDF p. 1).
quotes: "Autonomous driving behaviour may lead to confusion and negative user experience." (p. 1)

paper_code_entries.value: process — the study measures UX, understanding, ease of use, and perceived control during the interaction (PDF pp. 7–8).
quotes: "Overall, group B, where live explanations were provided, had higher ratings in ease of use and understanding of the system than group A." (p. 7)
"Providing passengers with live explanations during the ride also increases the feeling of control compared to the group that did not receive any information during the drive." (p. 8)

paper_code_entries.value: structuring — the display organizes intended route, detected objects, their status, and trip state into inspectable visual elements (PDF p. 4).
quotes: "Detected objects in the street and their status were also marked on the display if they were relevant for the driving situation." (p. 4)

paper_code_entries.value: distributed_support — explanatory support is spread across an in-ride display and a post-ride mobile application (PDF pp. 4, 9).
quotes: "Only the participants of group B received live explanations in multiple ways." (p. 4)
"Both groups, however, were able to interact with a mobile app that summarised the drive and explained the autonomous shuttle manoeuvres afterwards." (p. 9)

paper_code_entries.value: none_comparator_only — the explanatory graphics were manually authored rather than generated by the vehicle AI (PDF p. 10).
quotes: "Also, as the visual enhancements on the displays were done manually, the intended route and marked items were perfectly highlighted without errors." (p. 10)

paper_code_entries.value: pre_ai_computational — the scaffold’s meaning follows a manually authored conventional display-and-app path (PDF p. 10).
quotes: "Also, as the visual enhancements on the displays were done manually, the intended route and marked items were perfectly highlighted without errors." (p. 10)

limitations: "While the use of an AV simulator creates a better live experience than just a screen, it is still not a real driving situation." (PDF p. 10)
"Another aspect that has to be taken into account are the rather young participants with 25 years on average, which might be a reason for their positive attitude towards AVs." (PDF p. 10)

"The simulator did also lack some aspects to support an immersive experience: no driving noise was available during the experiment, no visual depth was provided by the displays, and the display visualisations only simulated augmented reality." (PDF p. 10)
"Also, as the visual enhancements on the displays were done manually, the intended route and marked items were perfectly highlighted without errors." (PDF p. 10)
"They did not intend to travel from one location to another." (PDF p. 10)
"Longitudinal studies can lead to further insights." (PDF p. 11)
"The additional hypothesis about a feeling of control, however, is not part of the AVAM and participants were only asked to answer one item." (PDF p. 10)
boundary_conditions: "This paper focusses on vehicles with full driving automation (SAE level 5 [43]) and investigates if system explanations can improve the UX during autonomous rides." (PDF p. 1)

"Based on their prior experiences with autonomous systems, participants are distributed in: 25% had no prior experiences, 50% had experiences with driving assistance such as cruise control, 12.5% had experiences with semi-automatic driving systems such as lane assists, 5% had experiences with highly automated driving systems such as highway and take-over driving assistants, and 7.5% had experiences with fully autonomous vehicles in research contexts." (PDF p. 3)
"The recorded driving situation took place in an urban downtown area during the daytime." (PDF p. 4)
